name: The Pioneer Woman Chili
writer_notes: Diced tomatoes: source labels the 14.5 oz diced tomatoes as Instant Pot version only and no stovetop step uses them, but the skeleton buys 34 oz with juice. To avoid an orphaned bought ingredient (spec-guards hard fail), I wrote one stovetop one-pot method that adds the diced tomatoes with juice during the hour simmer. Repair pass should confirm the build intended diced tomatoes in the recipe.
Method choice: the source has three methods (stovetop, crock pot, Instant Pot). I wrote a single stovetop method for the card and did not name the other appliances.
Source garnishes tortilla chips / Fritos and cornbread are not in the 16 locked buy lines, so I omitted them from all prose and steps and added them to forbidden_prose_terms.
Cost: no cost_ps or cost_lines were in the dispatch, so cost prose uses the ${{cost_ps}} token and shop_smart makes no package-tracing (per-ounce or lasts-several-batches) claims.
Macros within gate band: 680 cal (450-800) and 41.8 g protein (>= 40). Real carbohydrate source satisfied by beans, masa, and tomatoes (42.2 g carbs).
Cal and protein written as {{cal}}/{{protein}} tokens per templating guidance.

prose.intro_html: Chili is the meal prep MVP, and this one earns the title. It is The Pioneer Woman's chili built for a real week, a big pot of ground beef, two kinds of beans, and a little masa harina that thickens it into something that clings to the spoon instead of running off it. Fourteen containers out of one pot, right around {{cal}} calories and {{protein}} grams of protein a serving. That lands exactly where a dinner should land for a plan that keeps you honest.
prose.shop_smart:
Ground beef is the whole game here, so buy the 80/20 and do not apologize for it. The fat carries the flavor and the masa binds everything together, so you are not draining money down the sink. Grab the family pack if your store runs one, since you need close to five pounds for the batch.

Canned beans and canned tomato sauce are the quiet heroes of a cheap high protein dinner. Kidney and pinto both go in, drained and rinsed, and the diced tomatoes go in with their juice, so leave that can undrained. Masa harina lives near the flour or in the Latin foods aisle, white or yellow both work, and you only need a little over half a cup for the whole pot. The garnishes, cheddar, sour cream, lime, and green onions, are where you make a container feel like a restaurant bowl for pocket change.
prose.make_it:
Brown the ground beef in your biggest pot over medium heat, breaking it up as it cooks, then drain off the excess grease. You want it browned, not steamed, so give it room.

Add the diced garlic and the tomato sauce and cook for one minute, just enough to wake the garlic up. Now the seasonings all at once, the chili powder, cumin, oregano, salt, and cayenne. Stir until the meat is fully coated, then drop the heat to low.

Pour in the diced tomatoes with their juice, cover, and let it simmer for about an hour, stirring now and then. If it looks dry along the way, a splash of water sets it right. When the hour is up, whisk the masa harina with half a cup of water in a small bowl until smooth and stir it into the pot. That is what turns loose chili into real chili. Add the drained and rinsed kidney and pinto beans and simmer ten more minutes so they heat through and take on the flavor.

Taste it, add a little more masa or water until the consistency is where you like it, and you are done. Portion and garnish at serving time.
prose.portion_html:
Here is the honest way to get fourteen even servings. Weigh your empty pot before you cook, or know its weight, then weigh the full pot when the chili is done and subtract. Divide that number by fourteen and you have your target grams per container, no eyeballing and no arguing over who got the big scoop. Ladle to the number and you hit {{cal}} calories and {{protein}} grams of protein a serving.

Keep the garnishes off until you eat. Store the chili plain in the fourteen containers, then top each bowl with shredded cheddar, a spoon of sour cream, a scatter of green onions, and a squeeze of lime when you heat it up. Cheese and sour cream stirred into a batch on day one is a sad reheat by day four.
prose.cost_closing_html:
This is what a budget dinner is supposed to look like. Real beef, two kinds of beans, and enough of it to fill fourteen containers, all for ${{cost_ps}} a serving. That is drive through soda money for a bowl that actually feeds you, {{protein}} grams of protein and a stick to your ribs kind of full.

Run the math on your week. Fourteen dinners at ${{cost_ps}} each is the kind of number that makes a grocery budget behave, and it tastes like you tried a lot harder than you paid.
prose.upsell_html: One pot, fourteen dinners, and a membership that runs a dollar a month. If this chili saved you a single takeout order, it already paid for the year. Come get the rest of the plan.

head.description: The Pioneer Woman Chili made for meal prep. A big pot of 80/20 ground beef, kidney and pinto beans, and a masa harina thickener portioned into 14 high protein dinners at about {{cal}} calories and {{protein}} grams of protein each.

steps: Brown the ground beef in a large pot over medium heat, breaking it up as it cooks, then drain off the excess grease.
Add the diced garlic and the tomato sauce and cook for 1 minute.
Stir in the chili powder, cumin, oregano, salt, and cayenne until the meat is coated, then reduce the heat to low.
Add the diced tomatoes with their juice, cover, and simmer for 1 hour, stirring occasionally and adding a splash of water if it looks dry.
Whisk the masa harina with 1/2 cup water until smooth and stir it into the pot to thicken.
Add the drained and rinsed kidney and pinto beans and simmer 10 minutes, adjusting with more masa or water until the consistency is right.
Portion into 14 containers and top each serving with shredded cheddar, sour cream, diced green onions, and a squeeze of lime.
